after: ## Legal rules and other rules and norms
alt: Legal rules are made by a state authority, bind everyone, are enforced by the courts, change at an identifiable moment and are challenged through legal processes; other rules are made by groups, bind members, are enforced socially and change gradually. A golf club can expel a cheat, but only the state’s law can prosecute fraud. Smoking in enclosed workplaces moved from manners to an offence under the Health Act 2006.
caption: Importance or obedience does not make a rule legal; enforcement by the state does.

after: ## Legal rules and other rules and norms
alt: A rule is specific, like a 30 mph limit; a principle is broad, like “no one may profit from their own wrong”, and guides judges when rules run out. Austin saw law as a sovereign’s command backed by a sanction. Hart saw a legal system as primary rules of conduct united with secondary rules of recognition, change and adjudication, so a school rule is not law.
caption: Hart’s rule of recognition explains why a school rule is not law.

alt: A careless driver who injures a cyclist can face a criminal prosecution by the Crown Prosecution Service, with a verdict of guilty or not guilty and a sentence decided by the court, and a separate civil claim in negligence by the cyclist, who decides whether to sue and may settle, with an outcome of liable or not liable and damages. Because the standards of proof differ, the outcomes can differ.
caption: Same facts, two cases, different language and possibly different results.

after: ## Sources of law: custom, statute and common law
alt: Four tests for a local custom: existence since time immemorial (1189); exercise peaceably, openly and as of right; reasonableness and certainty; and consistency with statute. Mercer v Denne succeeded (drying nets); Simpson v Wells failed on time immemorial; Wolstanton failed as unreasonable.
caption: A custom must pass all four tests, and most modern claims fail.

after: ## Sources of law: custom, statute and common law
alt: Statute, including delegated legislation within its powers, is highest because of parliamentary supremacy and overrides the common law, which is made by judges through precedent (murder; Donoghue v Stevenson). The common law overrides custom, which survives only locally if every test is met. Example: the Law Reform (Year and a Day Rule) Act 1996 abolished a common law rule.
caption: Statute beats common law; common law beats custom.

alt: The model answer in four moves: the source and scope of a legal rule, its enforceability by the state, a contrast with a club’s dress code, and an example of a social rule becoming law under the Health Act 2006.
caption: Name a feature, explain it, contrast it, then ground it in an example.
